title: Pathway-model memories are robust to a wide range of stimulus strengths

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pathway-model memories are robust to a wide range of stimulus strengths

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the surveyed ODE pathway models, memory formation is robust to training stimuli of 10x, 50x and 100x baseline (most models kept the same number of memories and only 10% lost memories), and some models formed more memories with weaker stimulation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.2. Memory Effects Are Robust to Different Strengths of Stimulus

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We conclude that the memory properties are robust to a wide range of stimulus strengths, a desirable property for therapeutics, and also for functional linkages with other cell pathways during evolution.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.2. Memory Effects Are Robust to Different Strengths of Stimulus”. Scope: 35 ODE pathway models from BioModels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-09: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a finite, quantitative comparison across specified public models and stimulus strengths. It can be confirmed or refuted with routine reruns.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run each model at 10, 50, and 100 times baseline stimulation and compare memory counts per model. The reported retention, loss, and weaker-stimulation gains provide direct decision criteria.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Solver tolerances can affect borderline classifications.

Three large fold-change levels do not establish robustness outside that range.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.86
operationalizability: 0.97
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decision rule is a numerical comparison of memory counts across three stated amplitudes, and both the models and the evaluation code are public. Some ambiguity remains about how 'baseline' is scaled in the MATLAB files versus the prose. That is a finite reimplementation check, not a missing experiment.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeat the memory screen at stimulus amplitudes of 10, 50 and 100 times baseline and compare memory counts per model with the baseline screen. Most models keeping the same count, about 10 percent losing memories, and some gaining memories at weaker stimuli, would confirm the claim; widespread loss at higher amplitudes would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The full combinatorial screen at three amplitudes is computationally heavy.

The main methods text specifies clamping to each variable's observed max and min, so the 10x, 50x and 100x factors need to be matched in the code or supplement.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.58
data existence: 0.8
discriminating power: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.78
